subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Fractals and Nature's Code
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fractals and Nature's Code usable.

hook.text: A fern leaf repeats its shape at every scale. Zoom in on a coastline—same wiggles forever. Fractals.

buildup.text: Mandelbrot named fractals in 1975. They describe shapes that repeat infinitely—trees, rivers, lungs, lightning.

discovery.text: African villages are often built in fractal patterns—circular compounds inside circular fences inside circles.

twist.text: Medieval Europeans assumed nature was geometric. Africans recognized fractals centuries before Western math did.

climax.text: Fractals reveal that nature's complexity comes from simple rules repeated infinitely. The cosmos is recursive.

quiz.question: Who named fractals and formalized their mathematics?
